questions.explain: Semantic cache stores question→answer pairs served via vector lookup (threshold 0.97+ for factual answers, tenant-scoped); embedding cache keys deterministic vectors by SHA2_256 of model+text; result cache stores query results with invalidation.
options: Semantic cache (LLM answers, vector lookup), embedding cache (deterministic vectors), result cache (query results)
questions.q: What are the three AI caches and what does each save?

questions.explain: Embeddings are deterministic — the same text through the same model always yields the same vector — so key by hash of (model + text) and never pay twice; ~90% hit rate on document re-ingestion makes it the highest-ROI cache.
options: The embedding cache is the highest-ROI cache: deterministic embeddings keyed by hash of model+text, never computed twice
The embedding cache has no value
questions.q: Why is the embedding cache the highest-ROI cache?

questions.explain: Query Notifications where the query is notification-compatible; otherwise the Change Tracking poll loop doubles as the invalidation sweep (depends_on tables); TTLs as the backstop (5 min dashboards, 1 hour text-to-SQL).
options: Query Notifications where compatible, Change Tracking polling otherwise, TTLs as backstop

questions.explain: Every cache reports hit rate (below 20% → remove it), tokens/money saved (the budget justification), and staleness incidents (above zero for semantic cache → raise threshold or shorten TTLs); delete caches that don't earn their complexity.
options: Hit rate, tokens/money saved, and staleness incidents — delete caches that don't earn their complexity

questions.explain: Replay the top-N cached queries from the last 24 hours through the normal lookup path as an automated post-deploy job; the app must treat every cache as optional — a cold cache means slower responses, never errors.
options: Automated post-deploy warming (replay top-N queries); treat every cache as optional so cold starts degrade gracefully
questions.q: How are cold starts handled after deployments or failovers?
